source.edits: Remove spoken introduction, title and closing credits only. Preserve internal pauses. No time stretch, denoising, music or dynamic compression.
source.alignment: Approximate display-only word timestamps from faster-whisper 1.2.1 base.en; grouped against the printed lines. ASR transcript was not used as poem text and never enters encoder, simulator or interpretation. Boundaries need human listening review.

normalization.method: whole-waveform RMS, peak-limited linear gain; PCM16 quantization

encoder.mapping: min(4 * frame RMS, 0.8) equally into upstream ear_cells

response.units: spikes per second per neuron (Hz/neuron), unless stated otherwise

measurement_rules.transition_rule: outside max(3 baseline smoothed SD, 0.02 Hz/neuron) for 60 ms
measurement_rules.recovery_rule: first 200 ms continuously within that band; null = not observed in tail
measurement_rules.population_rank: absolute audio-minus-baseline mean Hz per neuron; no minimum group size
measurement_rules.warning: Descriptive single-run changes, not statistical significance or behavioral observations.

rules.control: Same seed, reset, duration and parameters; every auditory injection is zero.
rules.smoothing: Causal 100 ms mean for traces and peak; unsmoothed phase means for rates.
rules.ranking: Absolute poem minus matched silence mean Hz/neuron; includes small populations.
rules.limitation: One paired seed. A model counterfactual, not a population norm, significance test or evidence of language processing.

affect.text: This sounding raises mean network activity relative to its matched silence. Its strongest global departure arrives midway, at 29.82 seconds. Through an affect-theory lens, these differences invite attention to how an encounter alters an ongoing system: where a disturbance gathers force, travels, and leaves a remainder. The recorded aftermath differs from silence by +0.005 Hz per neuron. We read the trajectory as a relation made and altered in time, rather than assigning the fly a human emotion. A changed firing rate is evidence of perturbation; a changed capacity to act would require further experiments.
affect.scope: A situated critical interpretation, not an affect detector. Removing semantics by design does not prove affect is independent of meaning.

sources.title: Leys and interlocutors — Affect: An Exchange

functional_notes.label: Sensing vibration
functional_notes.role: These antennal sensory neurons respond to vibration and participate in hearing in living flies.
functional_notes.limit: We stimulate these neurons directly. Their increase checks the input bridge; it does not demonstrate recognition, attention or enjoyment.
functional_notes.measurement: 27,687 more spikes across 138 neurons over 45.10 seconds; +4.449 Hz/neuron against matched silence.

functional_notes.label: Beyond the sensory input
functional_notes.role: These neurons receive direct connections from the stimulated JONs in the connectome. This is a structural group with potentially mixed functions.
functional_notes.limit: A change here shows that activity differs beyond the injected neurons. It does not by itself establish a specific percept or behavioral response.
functional_notes.measurement: 11,273 more spikes across 1017 neurons over 45.10 seconds; +0.246 Hz/neuron against matched silence.

functional_notes.label: Signals toward motor circuits
functional_notes.role: Descending neurons link the brain with motor circuits in the ventral nerve cord. They support many different actions.
functional_notes.limit: A whole-group mean cannot identify an action. Opposing, lateralized or brief signals may disappear when averaged together.
functional_notes.measurement: 544 more spikes across 1314 neurons over 45.10 seconds; +0.009 Hz/neuron against matched silence.

functional_notes.label: Steering-related circuit
functional_notes.role: DNa02 belongs to descending circuitry associated with steering during walking.
functional_notes.limit: The pooled mean does not resolve left-right steering or establish that a turn would occur.
functional_notes.measurement: 6 fewer spikes across 2 neurons over 45.10 seconds; -0.067 Hz/neuron against matched silence.

functional_notes.label: Escape take-off circuit
functional_notes.role: DNp01 is the giant-fiber descending neuron associated with rapid escape take-off.
functional_notes.limit: A change in this model is an escape-circuit change, not evidence of fear or a predicted jump. No behavioral activation threshold is calibrated here.
functional_notes.measurement: No net change in total spikes across 2 neurons over 45.10 seconds.
functional_notes.inference: Total activity matched silence; temporal patterns can still differ.

functional_notes.label: Backward-walking circuit
functional_notes.role: Moonwalker descending neurons can recruit the motor circuitry for backward walking in living flies.
functional_notes.limit: A rate difference does not establish retreat, avoidance or a subjective wish to get away.
functional_notes.measurement: 4 fewer spikes across 4 neurons over 45.10 seconds; -0.022 Hz/neuron against matched silence.

functional_notes.label: Courtship-song production circuit
functional_notes.role: pIP10 descending neurons participate in driving the wing movements that produce courtship song.
functional_notes.limit: Activity here is not evidence of attraction, pleasure, or an actual song. Social context and cooperating circuits matter.
functional_notes.measurement: 1 fewer spike across 2 neurons over 45.10 seconds; -0.011 Hz/neuron against matched silence.

reading.scope: Circuit roles come from research; rate differences come from this model; experience is not measured.
reading.text: The voice enters through the modeled vibration-sensing pathway and carries beyond it: both the sensory neurons and their direct postsynaptic partners fire more than in silence. The strongest whole-network departure falls in the middle third, at 29.82 seconds. As a reading, this is contact and propagation: a patterned disturbance that travels, without a demonstrated destination in action. The recorded activity gives the encounter a sensory shape; it does not establish what, if anything, the fly feels.
reading.status: Interpretation of a model counterfactual, not cognition or observed behavior

interpretation_lenses.note: Circuit and affect lenses share this response-only summary; no poem text.

display.poem:
Little fly,
Thy summer’s play
My thoughtless hand
Has brushed away.

Am not I
A fly like thee?
Or art not thou
A man like me?

For I dance
And drink and sing,
Till some blind hand
Shall brush my wing.

If thought is life
And strength and breath,
And the want
Of thought is death,

Then am I
A happy fly,
If I live,
Or if I die.
